title: Camunda 7 overwrites prior variable state in place at its default history level
content:
The configuration documentation states it plainly: *"Rows in this table are updated as variable instances are updated, meaning that only the last value of a process variable will be available."* Recovering intermediate values requires opting up to the `FULL` history level, which is also where the user-attributed User Operation Log lives — so attribution is off by default too.

This is destructive in-place update presented as history. The engine is doing what it says, but a record that keeps only the latest value cannot answer what a decision looked like when it was taken.

It is also the strongest available demonstration against a Camunda 7 estate, because no API call is needed: a default installation destroys prior state on its own, as a consequence of normal operation.
description: At the default AUDIT level the historic variable row is updated rather than appended, so only the last value survives and intermediate states are gone.
